title: fix(mobile): report the declared spec gesture in every useSpecGesture fallback
body:
Fixes #9691

Clause-②: yes

`useSpecGesture` builds each `onGesture` fallback payload by spreading the recognizer's runtime context next to a declared `type`. That context carries a `type` of its own — `GestureContext.type`, the direction-fused recognizer vocabulary — so an arm that writes `type` BEFORE the spread has its declared value overwritten by the recognizer's. Three arms carried that order; `type` now goes last at all three, which is the spelling the `swipe` arm already uses.

Executed as one change per the triage ruling on the card (comment `5714886682`): 「三处是**同一个书写顺序缺陷**,⛔ 一起改;并顺手加一条断言把「展开在前、`type` 在后」钉住,否则第四处会以同样方式长出来。」

## The card's table, re-derived on this branch's base

The table on the card was measured on PR #9689's head. Re-derived on `origin/main` at `57c07f002` — every row holds, and the line numbers happen not to have moved:

| line | arm | spelling | declared `type` survives? |
|---|---|---|---|
| 117 | `swipe` | `{ ...ctx, type: 'swipe' }` | yes — spread first |
| 124 | `long_press` | `{ type: 'long_press' }` | yes — no `ctx` spread |
| 128 | `pinch` | `{ type: 'pinch', ...ctx }` | **no** |
| 132 | `double_tap` | `{ type: 'double_tap' }` | yes — no `ctx` spread |
| 137 | `pan` / `drag` | `{ type: declared, ...ctx }` | **no** |
| 141 | `rotate` | `{ type: 'rotate', ...ctx }` | **no** |

## One arm moves observably; the rest were latent

`drag` is the only configuration whose payload changes. It is the one arm where the two vocabularies disagree — `drag` declared, `pan` recognized — so it reported `pan`. `pinch`, `rotate` **and a declared `pan`** name their recognizer identically, so the overwrite replaced each value with itself. The changeset says exactly this rather than claiming three behaviour changes.

## The load-bearing runtime fact, pinned instead of probed

The card supported "`ctx` really carries a `type` key at runtime" with a throwaway probe that was then deleted. That fact is now a standing assertion — `useGesture`'s emitted context is asserted to carry the recognizer's own name. It passes on **both** sides of the repair by design and is not a witness; it is there so that removing `GestureContext.type` some day reds the file that depends on it, and the test says so in its own name and message.

## The ordering pin

`packages/mobile/src/__tests__/spec-gesture-fallback-type-order.test.tsx`, three kinds of pin, because no one kind covers the defect:

1. **the runtime fact** above;
2. **per-arm behaviour, driven with a DRIFTED recognizer context** — every one of the seven declared gestures is exercised with a context whose `type` has been moved off the declared name (`'tap'`, a real recognizer name that is no spec gesture's declared name). That drift is precisely the condition the card says a rename on either vocabulary creates, so it is how the quiet arms are made to speak. Without it, `pinch` and `rotate` pass identically on defect and fix;
3. **the writing order, read off the hook's source** — every `fallback(...)` payload is brace-matched out of `useSpecGesture.ts` and the spread is required to precede `type`. This is the part that answers the triage's 「否则第四处会以同样方式长出来」: a behavioural pin only guards arms somebody thought to list, this one guards the shape. It carries its own non-vacuity checks — the brace matcher must account for every `fallback(` call it finds, and at least one payload must actually spread — so a scanner that silently stops matching reds instead of going quietly green.

The behavioural rows are also a completeness pin: the row set is compared against `SPEC_GESTURE_TYPES`, so a new spec gesture cannot be added with a switch arm and no row.

## Shown RED before the repair

The pin was run against the unrepaired hook, then again after the fix was committed, with the mutation and the restore both proved by `git hash-object` against recorded blob hashes rather than by an exit code.

| leg | on-disk `useSpecGesture.ts` blob | result |
|---|---|---|
| without the fix | `489483d9dbb37431c3fc04bb4b7e2ea439f292d0` (the `origin/main` blob) | **6 failed, 35 passed (41)** |
| with the fix | `3dde33fc1cc89ed17dc7e60dce9dafa8575ebfd2` (this branch's HEAD blob) | **41 passed (41)** |

The six that go red are the whole defect and nothing else — the live instance, the four drifted-context arms, and the shape pin:

```
× a declared `drag` reports 'drag', not the recognizer's 'pan'
× pinch
× pan
× drag
× rotate
× spreads the recognizer context BEFORE writing `type`, at every site
```

with the two discriminating readings:

```
AssertionError: the DECLARED spec gesture — this is the one arm where the two
vocabularies disagree: expected "vi.fn()" to be called with arguments:
  - "type": "drag"
  + "type": "pan"
```

```
AssertionError: `type` goes LAST: ... expected [ … ] to deeply equal []
+ [
+   "{ type: 'pinch', ...ctx }",
+   "{ type: declared, ...ctx }",
+   "{ type: 'rotate', ...ctx }",
+ ]
```

`swipe`, `long_press` and `double_tap` pass on both sides and are kept anyway: the first is the arm PR #9689 already repaired and the other two spread nothing, so none of the three can tell the two implementations apart. Said here rather than left for a reader to discover.

The suite imports the hook by a RELATIVE source path from inside its own package, so the mutated file is unambiguously the one under test — no `dist` and no vitest alias sits between them.

## The fourth file, and why it is there

`packages/mobile/tsconfig.test.json` gains `"types": ["node"]`. The shape pin reads the hook's own source, and this package's test project named no `types`, so `node:fs` did not resolve (`TS2591`). Twenty-five sibling packages already declare it the same way, `packages/types` for the same reason (its re-export guard's `readFileSync`). Naming `types` switches off automatic `@types/*` inclusion, so the list is deliberately complete: these suites import no ambient matcher package. `tsc -p packages/mobile/tsconfig.test.json --listFiles` confirms the new test really is a program input rather than silently excluded.

## Adjacent, deliberately untouched

`SPEC_GESTURE_TYPE_MAP.swipe` is still `'swipe-left'` as a declared placeholder. Changing an exported map's VALUE is a published-surface change no card has ruled on, and this branch does not touch those lines.

Every exit code was redirected to a file and read from there, never through a pipe.

**ESLint is a declared narrowing, not a skip.** `pnpm exec eslint packages/mobile --format json` at `f38da33`: 21 files judged, 0 errors, 18 warnings, none of them in either file this branch writes. The narrowing is safe to make because this repo's flat config extends `tseslint.configs.recommended` with no `parserOptions.project` and no `projectService` — type-aware linting is off, so a file's verdict is a function of its own bytes and the shared config alone, and this branch adds no config, no shared file ESLint reads and no disable directive. It therefore cannot move the verdict of any file it does not touch. The repo-wide `pnpm lint` and the full sharded suite remain CI's.

Heavy runs were serialized through the shared verify lock.
